a1_answer:
PROPOSED INDICATOR AND THRESHOLD: Replace the retubing intervention with an online predictor that monitors the divergence between the condenser’s actual coolant outlet temperature and a dynamic, flow-normalized baseline temperature predicted from existing temperature and flow measurements only. The predictor fires a maintenance alert when the temperature divergence exceeds a set threshold, ensuring detection at least three weeks before back-pressure hits the derating limit. This approach uses only existing instrumentation to avoid false trips during load swings by normalizing for flow variations.

MECHANISM: Biofouling increases thermal resistance on the tube-side, causing the coolant outlet temperature to rise for a given heat duty. Since back-pressure is not an allowed signal, the predictor isolates the thermal degradation signature by comparing the measured coolant outlet temperature against a real-time baseline that accounts for steam exhaust heat duty (via flow measurements). This thermal drift serves as a leading indicator of heat transfer loss caused by biofilm formation.

DEPARTURE FROM STANDARD: The standard solution is periodic retubing with copper-nickel alloys (e.g., C70600), which is a material intervention rather than a predictor. The genuine departure here is the implementation of a purely software-based, online leading indicator that leverages existing thermal data to predict fouling onset without new hardware or material changes.

LABELED PARAMETERS:
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Baseline Calculation Method = Real-time flow-normalized heat duty correlation (your design choice; no citation, as no record specifies the exact baseline algorithm for this specific 300 MW unit)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: Sampling Rate = 1 Hz (your design choice; no citation, consistent with standard DCS capabilities)

INDICATOR: Coolant Outlet Temperature Divergence ($\Delta T_{dev}$) in °C
THRESHOLD: 1.5 °C (ASSUMPTION)

VALIDATION PROTOCOL: Temperature, duration: 30-day data window, sample size: n = 5 independent DEVICES (condensers). The protocol validates the Coolant Outlet Temperature Divergence ($\Delta T_{dev}$) by requiring a sustained threshold exceedance of 1.5 °C for 48 hours to confirm detection, filtering out transient load swing artifacts.
